title: Fits of 10 to 40 fast modes shift the KIC 10001893 14.261300 microHz coefficient by less than 1.2 ppm in 14 Kepler quarters
abstract: We test linear sampling leakage into the known 14.261300 microHz signal of KIC 10001893. We use 51,679 accepted exposures from 14 Kepler release 25 quarters. Each quarter has 10, 20 or 40 selected fast modes between 80 and 280 microHz. We fit these modes with the slow signal and local trends. Across two flux products and two trend lengths, the slow sine and cosine coefficient vector changes by 0.88 to 1.18 ppm. Its remaining amplitude is 30.79 to 33.50 ppm. An exact projection identity and synthetic signal tests pass. Thus the fitted fast modes explain only a small part of this slow coefficient through linear leakage. The result does not test omitted modes, nonlinear mixing, pixel extraction or all instrument effects. The frequency was selected in prior work on the same observations. The two flux products share exposures. No new signal or planet is confirmed. The bundle gives original code, aggregate fits, source hashes, a figure and external retrieval steps.

display.caption: The fast-mode fit changes the slow coefficient by about 1 ppm. The remaining amplitude exceeds 30 ppm. These fits do not identify its source.
